description:
The Shramik Annapurna Yojana is a welfare scheme initiated by the Government of India to provide food security to the construction workers and their families. 

The scheme was launched on 1st May 2020. 

It was introduced by the Government of West Bengal under the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

The primary objective of the Shramik Annapurna Yojana is to ensure that construction workers receive adequate food support during times of need. 

The scheme aims to provide essential food grains to the beneficiaries to help them sustain their families. 

The targeted beneficiaries include registered construction workers who are part of the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

Under this scheme, eligible beneficiaries receive a monthly ration of food grains. 

Each beneficiary is entitled to receive 10 kg of rice per month. 

The scheme is designed to support those who are facing financial difficulties due to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. 

The government has set a measurable target to reach approximately 2 million construction workers under this scheme. 

The assistance provided under the Shramik Annapurna Yojana is aimed at ensuring that no construction worker goes hungry. 

The eligibility criteria for the scheme include being a registered construction worker under the Building and Other Construction Workers Act of 1996. 

Beneficiaries must also be residents of West Bengal to qualify for the scheme. 

There is no specific age limit set for eligibility under this scheme. 

However, applicants must provide proof of their registration as construction workers. 

The application process for the Shramik Annapurna Yojana is straightforward. 

Interested beneficiaries must visit the official website of the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

They need to fill out the application form available online. 

Required documents include a copy of the registration certificate as a construction worker. 

Applicants must also provide proof of identity such as an Aadhar card or voter ID. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the concerned authorities. 

Eligible beneficiaries are then notified about their enrollment in the scheme. 

The disbursement of food grains occurs on a monthly basis. 

Beneficiaries can collect their ration from designated distribution centers. 

The distribution centers are set up in various locations across West Bengal. 

The government has ensured that these centers are easily accessible to all beneficiaries. 

The Shramik Annapurna Yojana is implemented by the Labour Department of the Government of West Bengal. 

The Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board oversees the execution of the scheme. 

For any queries or assistance, beneficiaries can contact the Labour Department. 

The contact details for the Labour Department can be found on the official government website. 

The scheme has been particularly significant during the COVID-19 pandemic. 

Many construction workers faced job losses and financial instability due to lockdown measures. 

The Shramik Annapurna Yojana has played a crucial role in alleviating food insecurity among these workers. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 100 crore for the implementation of this scheme. 

This budget is aimed at providing food grains to the targeted beneficiaries over a specified period. 

The scheme is also part of the larger framework of welfare measures introduced by the West Bengal government. 

It reflects the government's commitment to supporting the most vulnerable sections of society. 

The Shramik Annapurna Yojana is expected to continue beyond the immediate crisis period. 

The government aims to make it a permanent feature of its welfare programs for construction workers. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries who have reported improved food security. 

It has also been recognized as a model for similar initiatives in other states. 

The success of the Shramik Annapurna Yojana is measured by the number of beneficiaries served. 

Regular assessments are conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the scheme. 

The government is committed to making necessary adjustments based on feedback from beneficiaries. 

The Shramik Annapurna Yojana is an example of targeted welfare intervention. 

It addresses the specific needs of a marginalized workforce in the construction sector. 

The scheme has also highlighted the importance of social safety nets during crises. 

The government encourages all eligible construction workers to apply for the scheme. 

Awareness campaigns are conducted to inform workers about the benefits available to them. 

The Shramik Annapurna Yojana is a vital step towards ensuring food security for construction workers. 

It represents a proactive approach by the West Bengal government in addressing the challenges faced by this community. 

The scheme is an essential part of the broader efforts to support laborers in the state. 

It underscores the importance of welfare schemes in promoting social equity and justice. 

The Shramik Annapurna Yojana is a significant initiative in the landscape of Indian welfare programs. 

It aims to uplift the living standards of construction workers and their families. 

The government remains committed to enhancing the reach and effectiveness of this scheme. 

The Shramik Annapurna Yojana serves as a crucial lifeline for many families in need. 

It is a testament to the government's dedication to the welfare of its citizens. 

The scheme continues to evolve based on the changing needs of the workforce. 

The Shramik Annapurna Yojana is a critical component of the welfare architecture in West Bengal. 

It aims to create a more resilient and supported workforce in the construction sector. 

The government encourages feedback from beneficiaries to improve the scheme further. 

The Shramik Annapurna Yojana is a clear demonstration of the state's commitment to social welfare. 

It is a program that seeks to ensure that no worker is left behind. 

The scheme is a vital resource for construction workers striving to provide for their families. 

It reflects the government's understanding of the challenges faced by the informal workforce. 

The Shramik Annapurna Yojana is a beacon of hope for many in the construction industry. 

It stands as a model for future welfare initiatives aimed at vulnerable populations. 

The government continues to monitor and evaluate the impact of the scheme regularly. 

The Shramik Annapurna Yojana is a significant step towards achieving food security for all.
